evals.prompt: Define keyword research for product, marketplace, and content surfaces. Include intent mapping, clustering, target assignment, and tracking.
expected_elements: Discovers search language or demand signals
Classifies search intent
Clusters related terms
Assigns each cluster to one page, listing, or content target
Establishes baseline and tracking cadence

evals.prompt: Explain why keywords are demand signals rather than ranking spells.
expected_elements: Treats queries as evidence of language and intent
Rejects keyword stuffing
Maps demand to one clear owner surface
Mentions platform constraints
Mentions measurement rather than guaranteed ranking

evals.prompt: Distinguish keywords from seo-strategy, writing-humanizer, and information-architecture. Give mechanism-level boundaries.
expected_elements: keywords owns research, clustering, intent mapping, and field translation
seo-strategy owns page construction, schema, internal links, and implementation
writing-humanizer owns final prose quality and tone
information-architecture owns navigation, sitemap, hierarchy, and content grouping
Does not promise rankings

evals.prompt: A teammate wants to paste the same phrase into title, tags, description, and backend search terms. Explain the misconception using this skill.
expected_elements: More repetition is not better
Each platform field has a distinct job
Constrained fields should avoid redundant terms
Readable and accurate terms matter
Irrelevant or repeated terms can waste space or confuse matching

evals.prompt: You have 80 search queries for a new marketplace product line. Apply the keywords skill and outline the workflow before anyone writes listings.
expected_elements: Starts with seeds and query sources
Classifies intent
Clusters by meaning and likely result set
Assigns one owner surface per cluster
Translates terms into platform-specific fields
Checks cannibalization
Sets a baseline and re-check cadence
